newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN LENDING RATE RISES TO 10 PCT, DEMAND POOR.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN LENDING RATE RISES TO 10 PCT, DEMAND POOR.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate rose to 10 percent on Wednesday from 9.3 percent, despite poor demand and total trade was down by roughly a third from Tuesday at a meagre 22.4 million kuna.
Fresh loans accounted for 13.7 million kuna.

The interbank call money rate was unchanged at 7.0 percent. Term borrowings were granted at between 7.0 percent for rolled-over one-week insurer funds and 18 percent charged for 61-day deals with savings banks.
Kuna midrates for Thursday firmed to 3.5574 against the dollar and to 6.5830 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
